Government Of Canada Scholarships 2026 Now Open (Fully Funded) Government Of Canada Scholarships 2026 Now Open (Fully Funded) Gagandeep Kaur Sekhon 17 February 2026, 9:57 AM EST 17 February 2026, 12:19 PM EST Canada Immigration News , International Students , Study Permit Canada Last Updated On 17 February 2026, 12:19 PM EST (Toronto Time) The Government of Canada has officially opened applications for the Canadian Government Scholarships 2026, offering fully funded opportunities for international students to study and conduct research at Canadian universities and colleges. Administered through Global Affairs Canada and EduCanada, these prestigious scholarship programs provide comprehensive financial support covering living expenses, airfare, health insurance, and visa fees for students from eligible countries around the world. Canada continues to rank among the top destinations for international education, combining world-class academic institutions with multicultural communities and exceptional quality of life. The Canadian government scholarships for 2026 represent a strategic investment in developing human capital and strengthening international partnerships through educational exchange. Whether you are pursuing undergraduate studies, a master’s degree, or PhD research, these scholarship opportunities provide a pathway to gain valuable Canadian educational experience without the burden of tuition fees. The Study in Canada Scholarships program, Emerging Leaders in the Americas Program, and the newly expanded SEED-2 initiative collectively support students from over 60 countries across Latin America, the Caribbean, Africa, Asia, and Europe. Each program operates under distinct eligibility criteria and application procedures, yet all share the common goal of fostering international collaboration while providing exceptional educational opportunities in Canada. Table of Contents Overview of Canadian Government Scholarships 2026 The Canadian government scholarships 2026 encompass three primary funding streams administered by Global Affairs Canada through EduCanada. These programs are specifically designed to support short-term study and research exchanges at Canadian post-secondary institutions, enabling international students to gain valuable academic experience while maintaining enrollment at their home universities . Unlike traditional scholarships where students apply directly, the Canadian government scholarships operate through a unique institutional model. Canadian colleges and universities must apply on behalf of eligible students through the My EduCanada portal. This approach ensures quality control and facilitates the establishment of meaningful institutional partnerships between Canadian schools and their international counterparts. The three main scholarship programs accepting applications for the 2026-2027 academic year include the Study in Canada Scholarships for students from select countries in Asia, Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and Sub-Saharan Africa, the Emerging Leaders in the Americas Program for students from Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development Phase 2 program for students from ASEAN member states, Pacific Island Countries, and Mongolia. Study in Canada Scholarships 2026 The Study in Canada Scholarships program represents Global Affairs Canada’s flagship initiative for students from select regions worldwide. This fully funded scholarship supports short-term study or research exchanges at Canadian post-secondary institutions, with applications currently open for the 2026-2027 academic cycle. According to EduCanada, the Study in Canada Scholarships offer Canadian post-secondary institutions the opportunity to host international students from a diverse range of countries and territories for short-term study or research exchanges. Funded through the Academic Relations program, this initiative aims to strengthen and diversify Canada’s international linkages and partnerships while creating new connections that enrich educational engagement with global partners. Eligible Countries for Study in Canada Scholarships 2026: Asia: Bangladesh, Nepal, Taiwan Europe: Türkiye, Ukraine Middle East and North Africa: Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia Sub-Saharan Africa: Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda Students must be citizens of an eligible country and enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in that country, paying tuition fees to their home institution at the time of application and throughout their exchange period in Canada. Emerging Leaders in the Americas Program 2026 The Emerging Leaders in the Americas Program, commonly known as ELAP, enables eligible Canadian post-secondary institutions to award scholarships to students from Latin America and the Caribbean. Established by the Government of Canada in 2009, this program aims to foster the development of human capital and the next generation of leaders in the region while strengthening institutional partnerships and deepening people-to-people ties between Canada and the Americas. ELAP scholarships are offered to students from Caribbean, Central American, and South American countries who wish to pursue short-term studies or research in Canada. The program advances Canada’s education relations and engagement in Latin America and the Caribbean by providing funding for Canadian institutions to support international students from the region. Eligible Countries for ELAP 2026: Caribbean: Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Cuba, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos Central America: Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama South America: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Venezuela SEED-2 Scholarships 2026 The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development Phase 2 program, or SEED-2, represents an expansion of the original Canada-ASEAN SEED program and serves as a key initiative under Canada’s Indo-Pacific Strategy. Global Affairs Canada launched this expanded program in January 2026, extending eligibility to students from Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia in addition to ASEAN member states. The SEED-2 program provides opportunities for students to conduct short-term study or research in Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas that contribute to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Applications must demonstrate alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals and show how the proposed research or studies will help reduce poverty and narrow the development gap in eligible regions. Eligible Countries for SEED-2 2026: ASEAN Member States: Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, The Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Vietnam Pacific Island Countries: Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Other: Mongolia Scholarship Value and Financial Coverage The Canadian government scholarships 2026 provide substantial financial support to help international students focus on their academic pursuits without financial burden. The scholarship value varies depending on the duration of study or research and the academic level of the recipient. Study in Canada Scholarships Funding: CAD $10,200 for 4 months or one academic term for study or research at the college or undergraduate level CAD $10,200 for 4 months or one academic term for study or research at the graduate level (Master’s and PhD) CAD $14,000 for 5 to 6 months for study or research at the graduate level (Master’s and PhD) Emerging Leaders in the Americas Program Funding: CAD $8,200 for college, undergraduate, or graduate students (Master’s and PhD) for four months or one academic term of study or research CAD $11,100 for graduate students (Master’s and PhD) for a period of five to six months of study or research SEED-2 Program Funding: CAD $10,200 for graduate students for a minimum of four months of research CAD $12,700 for graduate students for a period of five to six months of research Expenses Covered by Canadian Government Scholarships: The scholarship funds are intended to cover essential costs associated with studying in Canada, including: Round-trip airfare to Canada by the most direct and economical route Health insurance coverage for the duration of the exchange Visa and study or work permit fees Living expenses including accommodation, food, and utilities Local transportation costs Books and academic supplies required for study or research (excluding computers and other equipment) Additionally, Canadian host institutions receive CAD $500 per implemented scholarship to cover administrative costs, including any employer compliance fees paid to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada if applicable. Important Note on Tuition Fees: These scholarships operate on an exchange model where tuition fees are handled differently than traditional scholarships. Students continue to be enrolled at and pay tuition to their home institution abroad. Canadian host institutions must waive tuition fees for scholarship recipients. This means you will not pay tuition to the Canadian school while participating in the exchange program, and the academic credits you earn in Canada will count towards your studies at your home institution. Eligibility Requirements for Canadian Government Scholarships 2026 To qualify for the Canadian government scholarships 2026, applicants must meet specific eligibility criteria established by Global Affairs Canada. While each program has distinct requirements, several common criteria apply across all three scholarship streams. General Eligibility Requirements: Must be a citizen of an eligible country or territory (citizenship requirements are strictly enforced) Must be enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country Must be paying tuition fees to the home institution at the time of application and for the full duration of the exchange in Canada Must be able to complete all project activities by September 30, 2027 Applicants Are Not Eligible If They: Hold Canadian citizenship or permanent residency, or have a pending application for either status Are already holding another grant or funding from Global Affairs Canada or from Canadian federal granting agencies such as NSERC, SSHRC, or CIHR Are already enrolled in a degree, diploma, or certificate program at a Canadian post-secondary institution Have previously received a scholarship under the same program (for SEED-2 participants) Documentation Requirements: Applicants must provide the following supporting documents as part of their application: Valid passport or national identity card with photo and valid dates (driver’s license, permanent residence card, work permit, student card, health card, and birth certificate are not accepted as proof of citizenship) Letter of proof of full-time enrollment from the home institution confirming current enrollment in a full-time program Letter of support from the home institution explaining the nature of study or research to be undertaken in Canada and how the candidate and home institution will benefit Academic transcripts For graduate students conducting research: Letter of invitation from the Canadian supervisor (maximum one page) Privacy Notice Statement signed by the candidate and dated within the last 6 months All documents in languages other than English or French must be accompanied by certified translations.
